na4mekku: mekku-stone; a mineral, frit or raw glass used in the production of glass and as an amulet stone.
merrutu: probably a medicinal plant; see CMAwR 1, text 1.1, 1.: 28′ and text 2.2, 1.: 130′′′′.
mēsu (gišMES): mēsu-wood; unidentified fruit tree native to Mesopotamia; the identification as hackberry is only based on etymology (cf. Bauer, OBO 160/1, 537).
úmirānu: mirānu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
munziqu (GEŠTIN.ḪÁD.A): raisin.
murdudû (ú/gišMUR.DÙ.DÙ): murdudû-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
šim?murrān: only in CMAwR 1, text 10.3: 45′; certainly identical with murrānu, an oil-producing tree or shrub.
murru (šimSES): ‘myrrh’; probably not true myrrh in most contexts; see CAD M II 221 and Jursa, Studies Sima, 163.
musukkannu (gišMES.MÁ.GAN.NA): rosewood; imported tree identified with Dalbergia sissoo (cf. Tengberg – Potts, AAE 10 [1999] 131–32).
na4mūṣu: mūṣu-stone; for mūṣu “bilharzia” and (na4)mūṣu “calculus discharged from the urinary passage”, see Kinnier Wilson, JNES 27 (1968) 24546, Herrero, RA 69 (1975) 49–50 and SchusterBrandis, Steine, 431–32.
muššaru (na4NÍR.MUŠ.GÍR): muššaru-stone; a stone with red and white stripes (banded agate); see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 433.
únab/mruqqu: nab/mruqqu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
nibu: see (yā)nibu.
nikiptu (ŠIM.dMAŠ/dNIN.URTA): nikiptu-plant; unidentified aromatic, gum-yielding plant, possibly a Euphorbia shrub (spurge).

nīnû (úKUR.RA): nīnû-plant; unidentified plant, used in medical contexts and as a spice. Based on Aramaic and Syriac cognates, Campbell Thompson, DAB, 67–69, suggested an identification as Ammi (bishop’s weed); Kinnier Wilson, JNES 64 (2005) 50–51 argues for an identification with mint.
nuḫurtu (úNU.LUḪ.ḪA): nuḫurtu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant, often used against witchcraft; according to Campbell Thompson, DAB, 353–59, to be identified with Asafoetida.
úNU.LUḪ: NU.LUḪ-plant; unidentified medicinal plant; possibly an alternative spelling of tīyatu (úKU.NU.LUḪ.ḪA), distinguished from, but associated with nuḫurtu (úNU.LUḪ.ḪA); cf. CMAwR 1, text 7.10.1, 1.: 95′′ and the commentary on text 1.1, 1.: 22′.
nurmû (gišNU.ÚR.MA): pomegranate.
únuṣābu: nuṣābu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
pallišu (na4NÍG.BÙR.BÙR): drilling stone; probably to be identified with emery; see SchusterBrandis, Steine, 435.
pappardilû (na4(NÍR.)BABBAR.DIL): (nir)pappardilû-stone; a black stone with one white stripe; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 403–4.
papparḫû (úBABBAR.ḪIsar): a garden plant; a possible Syriac cognate suggests an identification with purslane.
papparminû (na4BABBAR.MIN5): papparminûstone; a black stone with two white stripes; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 404.
pappasītu (BA.BA.ZA.(d)ÍD): pappasītu-mineral; a kind of sulphur, explained as kibrītu peṣītu “white sulphur” in a commentary text.
parzillu (AN.BAR), na4AN.BAR: iron; when determined by NA4 (‘iron stone’) it designates an iron bead (or perhaps a stone bead whose appearance is similar to iron).
pillû (ú/gišNAM.TAR/TAL): pillû-plant; medicinal plant, the identification with mandrake (so Campbell Thompson, DAB, 217–19) remains uncertain.
pindû (na4ŠE.TIR): pindû-stone; a mottled type of limestone; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 443–44.
piriggunû (na4PÌRIG.GÙN.A): piriggunû-stone; see Steinkeller, ZA 77 (1987) 92–95, Civil, Ebla 19751985, 151.
pû (IM.BUBBU): chaff.
úpuquttu: puquttu-thorn.
qadūt šikani (IM.GÚ.EN.NA): river sediment.
qan appāri: ‘marsh’-reed; a variety of reed.
qan-šalāli (GI.ŠUL.ḪI): šalālu-reed; a variety of reed.
qanû ṭābu (GI DU10.GA): ‘sweet’ reed; a variety of ‘reed’; cf. Jursa, Studies Sima, 163–64.
qaran ayyali: ‘stag’s horn’.
qutru (úKI.dIŠKUR): qutru-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
qunātā: woad.
rapādu, rapaddu: rapādu-plant; an unidentified steppe plant with blue-purple flowers; it is used both as a poison and a medicine (see CMAwR 2, text 7.24).
ruʾtītu (ÚḪ.dÍD): ruʾtītu-sulphur, explained by a commentary as kibrītu aruqtu “green (or: yellow) sulphur”.
na4sābu: sābu-stone; a red stone with apotropaic properties; also used for a precious mosaic pavement in the Neo-Assyrian period; see SchusterBrandis, Steine, 439–40.
úSAG: SAG-plant; unidentified medicinal plant; equated with la-a-ar-tu in Ḫḫ XVII (MSL 10, 108: 25, CAD L 103a), therefore lardu-grass?
saḫḫû: saḫḫû-mineral; an unidentified mineral or stone; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 441.
saḫlû (ZÀ.ḪI.LIsar): cress(?); a garden-plant, identification not entirely certain. For a full discussion, see Stol, JEOL 28 (1983–84) 24–32; but cf. the objections raised by Köcher, AUWE 10, 212.
samīdu (úKUR.ZI): samīdu-plant; unidentified vegetable, spice and medicinal plant.
sāmtu (na4GUG): literally “red (stone)”, here conventionally translated as “carnelian”, even though the use of the name is not restricted to carnelian.
úsibbirru, simbirru: sibbirru-plant; an unidentified medicinal plant and spice, associated with šibburratu in pharmaceutical texts.
giš/úsīḫu, šīḫu: sīhu-plant; an aromatic plant (shrub or tree?) and its resin; the identification with wormwood is based on etymology alone.
sikillu (úSIKIL): sikillu-plant, literally “the pure (herb)”; unidentified medicinal plant. Uruanna I 6 associates sikillu with maštakal-soapwort, ibid. I 19 sikillu is designated as “soapwort of the mountain(s)” (maltakal šadî). Šammu šikinšu notes that its leaves are similar to those of the ḫašḫūr api (STT 93 obv. 46′–47′, see Stadhouders, JMC 18 [2011] 9 § 19′).

siparru (ZABAR): bronze; bronze bead.
sû (na4ŠU.SAL.LA): sû-stone; probably red sandstone (see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 442–43); for the logogram na4ŠU.SAL.LA, see CMAwR 2, text 10.9, note on line 9′.
suādu (šimMAN.DU, in CMAwR 1, text 2.1, 1.: 138′′′′ šimIM.DU): suādu-plant; an aromatic plant; probably to be identified with chufa (yellow nutsedge).
suḫuššu (gišGIŠIMMAR.TUR): palm shoots.
suluppū (ZÚ.LUM.MA): date(s).
supālu (gišZA.BA.LAM; úNIGINsar in CMAwR 1, text 2.5, 1.: 12′): supālu-juniper; probably a variety of juniper.
ṣarbatu (gišÁSAL): poplar.
úṣaṣumtu (ṣaṣuttu): ṣaṣumtu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant; according to BAM 1 obv. II 3 //, one of the drugs effective against ašû-disease, but mentioned side by side with šammi ašî in CMAwR 1, text 7.10.1, 1.: 65′′, 73′′.
ṣumlalû (šimGAM.MA): ṣumlalû-spice; an unidentified spice and aromatic plant.
ṣurru (na4ZÚ): obsidian; varieties: ṣurru arqu “yellow obsidian”; ṣurru namru “light obsidian”; ṣurru ṣalmu “dark obsidian”.

šadânu ṣābitu (na4KA.GI.NA DAB.BA): magnetite; regarded as a stone of truth (cf. the Sumerian name), used especially for gaining favour; cf. SchusterBrandis, Steine, 424–25.
šakirû (úŠAKIRA): šakirû-plant; unidentified plant, mostly attested in medical contexts. A possible Syriac cognate suggests an identification with henbane.
šammi ašî: ašû-disease-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
šammi balāṭi (Ú.NAM.TI.LA): ‘plant-of-life’ (translation of the Sumerian and Akkadian name); unidentified medicinal plant.
šammi Lamašti: Lamaštu-plant (translation of the Akkadian name); unidentified medicinal plant.
šammi ṣerri (Ú MUŠ):‘snake’-plant (translation of the Sumerian and Akkadian name); unidentified medicinal plant.
šammu matqu: ‘sweet herb’ (translation of the Akkadian name); unidentified medicinal plant associated with ariḫu.
šammu peṣû (Ú.BABBAR): ‘white plant’ (translation of the Sumerian and Akkadian name); according to Uruanna I 226–27 a designation of the resin of the Euphrates poplar.
šammu ṣalmu (Ú GE6): ‘black plant’ (translation of the Sumerian and Akkadian name); unidentified medicinal plant which, according to Uruanna and similar plant lists, is to be identified with the aktamplant (see CAD A 282).
šarmadu (úGUR5.UŠ): šarmadu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
šaršerru (IM.SA5): red paint, paste; a red clay often used as a pigment.
šebirbirredû (ŠE.BIR.BIR.RE.DA): šebirbirredûbarley; possibly hulled barley, often used in purification rites (see CAD Š II 250–51).
šeguššu (ŠE.MUŠ5): šeguššu-barley.
šēp āribi: ‘crow’s foot’; unidentified medicinal plant.
šeʾu (ŠE): barley.
šibburratu (úLUḪ.MAR.TU): šibburratu-plant; unidentified medicinal plant; a possible Syriac cognate suggests an identification with rue.
šimbizidû (na4ŠIM.BI.ZI.DA): šimbizidû-mineral; a dark mineral that is used as an ingredient for eye makeup.
úšimru: šimru-fennel; cf. urânu and Ú.KU6.
šinni pīri (ZÚ AM.SI): ivory.
gišŠITA → bukānu.
šubû (na4ŠUBA): šubû-stone; material used for beads and seals; according to Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 446, rather a shell or a cowry snail than a mineral; variety: šubû seḫru “‘bent’ šubû-stone”.
šūmu, šūmū (SUMsar): garlic (bulb).
šumuttu (úSUMUN.DAR): beetroot(?); a field and garden plant well known for its red colour and associated with blood; its identification with beetroot is not entirely certain.
šunû (gišŠE.NÁ.A): chaste tree(?).
šupuḫru (gišEREN.BAD): šupuḫru-cedar; a variety of cedar.
šurdunû (úSI.SÁ): šurdunû-plant; unidentified medicinal plant, possibly rocket.
šurmēnu (gišŠUR.MÌN): cypress.

1. BOTANICAL AND MINERAL SUBSTANCES USED IN THE PRESCRIPTIONS 515
šuršummū šikari: beer dregs.
šūšu (gišŠE.DÙ): licorice (tree).
útarmuš: lupine; identification based on Aramaic and Arabic cognates, see Campbell Thompson, DAB, 125–26. CAD T 239a points out that “the plant’s description as šammi nipši points to a plant propagated by airborne seeds”; but nipšu may well refer to the characteristic smell of the plant.
taskarinnu (gišTAŠKARIN): boxwood.
terinnatu (gišŠE.Ù.SUḪ5): conifer cone.
tērītu: silt.
tiālu (gišEREN.BABBAR): white cedar.
tittu (gišPÈŠ): fig(-tree).
útiskur: tiskur-plant; unidentified medicinal plant.
tīyatu (úKU.NU.LUḪ(.ḪA)): tīyatu-plant; unidentified plant, used in medical contexts and as a spice, regularly combined and associated with nuḫurtu; cf. the commentary on CMAwR 1, text 1.1, 1.: 22′.
útullal: tullal-plant; unidentified medicinal plant. The name was interpreted as Akkadian tullal “you purify”; it is associated with maštakal-soapwort in Uruanna I 4–5.
turminabandû (na4DUR.MI.NA.BÀN.DA): turminabandû-breccia; a dark stone, see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 406.
turminû (na4DUR.MI.NA): turminû-breccia.
turû (SUM.ŠIR.DILI): turû-garlic, probably singleclove garlic.
ṭābat amanni (MUN a-ma-nim): amannu-salt; a red variety of salt, see Streck, RlA 11 (2008) 593.
ṭābat emesalli (MUN eme-sal-lim): emesallu-salt; a variety of salt, literally “salt of the fine tongue”.
ṭābat kupad (MUN kù/ku-pad): kupad-salt; a variety of salt; cf. Köcher, AUWE 10, 212. For the syllabic spelling ṭà-⌈ab⌉-ti ku-pa-ad, see CMAwR 1, text 2.1, 1.: 1 (OB). For KÙ.PAD.DU/DA = šibirtu “lump”, see CAD Š II 379.
ṭābtu (MUN): salt.
ṭūru (šimḪAB): ṭūru-resin; probably opopanax; cf. Jursa, Studies Sima, 166.
*(giš)Ú.GÍR.LAGAB: in CMAwR 1, text 7.10.1, 1.: 76′′′ read probably KIŠI16.ḪAB (see dādānu).
ÚḪ A.AB.BA: ‘spittle-of-the-sea’ (translation of the Sumerian name); unidentified mineral; probably to be read illāt tâmti in Akkadian, see commentary on CMAwR 1, text 1.1, 1.: 123′′′′′′.
uḫultu: soda ash; designates salt-plants and their alkaline ashes.
uḫūlu (NAGA): potash; designates salt-plants and their alkaline ashes.
(uḫūlu) qarnānû (NAGA SI): ‘horned’ salt-plant; probably a variety of Salicornia.
Ú.KU6: Ú.KU6-fennel (a literal translation of the logogram is perhaps ‘fish’-plant); a variety of fennel, Akkadian reading and exact relationship to urânu and šimru unknown.
uqnû (na4ZA.GÌN): here conventionally translated as “lapis lazuli”, even though the name is not restricted to lapis lazuli proper, but can refer to other blue stones as well.
uqūru (gišŠÀ.GIŠIMMAR): palm-heart.
urânu, urânnu (úTÁL.TÁL): urânu-fennel?; a vegetable and medicinal plant, probably a variety of fennel.
úurnû: urnû-plant; unidentified medicinal plant; the association with (a)naniḫu may suggest an identification with Ammi (probably not mint, as suggested by Campbell Thompson, DAB, 77–79).
ušû (gišESI): ebony.
na4yānibu: yānibu-‘stone’; a shell or cowry snail; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 421.
zagindurû (na4ZA.GÌN.DURU5): zagindurû-stone; a variety of lapis lazuli with a greenish hue; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 455.
zalāqu (na4ZÁLAG): zalāqu-stone; a light-coloured stone.
na4zibītu: zibītu-stone; an unidentified mineral, perhaps a shell; see Schuster-Brandis, Steine, 456.
